🌳ORCHARD ECONOMICS
LifecycleCostsBalance sheetInsuranceRWASources
🌳 RWA · Farm enterprise / balance sheet / insurance

An orchard is a capital project that grows.

Land, trees, water systems and years of establishment spending precede mature output. Orchard Economics turns that lifecycle into costs, cash flow, asset value, break-even conditions and insurable risk.

$17,292/ac3-year establishment cost · sample [1]
$42,292/acLand + establishment basis · sample [1]
$4,546/acTotal cash cost at 2,200 lb/ac [1]
$8,615/acTotal cost incl. capital recovery [1]
Sample, not universalThe model structure matters more than pretending one California budget prices every orchard.

Land, water, labor, variety, age, yield and financing differ materially by place and farm.

01 · LIFECYCLE

Capital comes before yield

The 2024 UC study assumes no crop in years 1–2, 500 lb/acre in year 3 and 2,200 lb/acre from year 6 onward.

Establishment: accumulated net cash establishment cost reaches $17,292/acre by year 3. The study amortizes it beginning in year 4 over the remaining 22 production years. [1]
02 · MATURE YEAR

What one modeled acre costs

At 2,200 lb/acre, cash cost and full economic cost diverge because the study includes capital recovery on land, establishment and equipment.

The sample assumes 2,200 kernel lb/acre. At $1.60/lb, gross revenue is $3,520 and return above cash cost is −$1,026/acre.

These are scenario points from the study's ranging analysis, not forecasts. [1]

03 · BALANCE SHEET

The orchard as an economic object

“Nut Balance Sheet” belongs here because an orchard mixes property, biological productive capital, seasonal working capital and debt.

Sample asset basis

Land$25,000/ac

Study's irrigated-site assumption.

Establishment$17,292/ac

Capitalized establishment cost.

The study explicitly notes $25,000 + $17,292 = $42,292 as consistent with an established mature-orchard basis in its sample. [1]

Conceptual balance sheet

AssetsLiabilities / claims
Land & water infrastructureMortgage / term debt
Trees / capitalized establishmentEquipment debt
Standing crop / inventoryOperating line / payables
Receivables / off-take claimsLiens / taxes / obligations
Insurance receivable if triggeredEquity residual
04 · RISK / INSURANCE

Insurance belongs inside the orchard model

It changes expected loss and lender protection; it is not a separate commodity layer.

Insurance price elections are not futures prices or forecasts. [2]

05 · RWA

The orchard is long-duration collateral; the crop is short-duration collateral.

Land/tree value, expected crop cash flow, harvested inventory and receivables have different duration, verification and liquidation properties.

LandSlow, durable, appraisal-driven.
TreesBiological productive capital.
CropSeasonal yield and price risk.
InventoryWarehouse/custody claim after harvest.

Risk domains

Drought, groundwater constraints, frost/heat, fire, pests/disease, alternate bearing, input inflation, market price, trade disruption and financing cost. Insurance only covers defined perils and terms; it does not erase enterprise risk.

Sources

Data registry

The orchard figures are study assumptions and observed insurance-program statistics, not universal market prices.

[1] UC Cooperative Extension / UC Davis · 2024 Almond Sample Costs, San Joaquin Valley North ↗100-acre conventional sample budget: land, establishment, yield, costs, capital recovery and ranging analysis.
[2] USDA RMA · PM-25-073: 2026 Almond Additional Price Elections ↗Conventional and organic additional/established price elections for crop insurance.
[3] USDA RMA · 2023 Specialty Crops Report Appendix ↗2022 insured acres, NASS acres and crop-insurance market penetration.
[4] USDA RMA · Summary of Business ↗Historical crop-insurance participation, premium and indemnity reporting.
